title: Waiver Watch List
brief: Which undrafted players should we watch in the first weeks for role, minutes or starting changes that make them worth a FAB bid? Each line must state the trigger that would make us add him.
summary: None of these players is worth real auction money. A few are worth 1 USD as last picks. The rest we track from day one and claim only when a set trigger happens: a new starting job, a jump in minutes, or a long-term injury to the player ahead of him. Bid quickly on lasting role changes. Use small bids or streams for short injury fill-ins.

paragraphs.text: Coaches do odd things in weeks one and two. Watch for surprise minutes, new starters, depth chart changes and players doing more. React fast to a real role change, such as a 28-minute starting role. Do not react to bad shooting nights if role, minutes and usage have not changed.

In our league, every name below sits at the edge of our 144-player pool or outside it. Spend nothing on them at the 2026-10-18 auction, or at most 1 USD on a last pick. Our waivers process daily. So in the first two weeks, check starting lineups and box score minutes every day and put in claims as soon as a trigger shows up. The waiver wire matters as much as the draft.

The notes pull in two directions. One side says react quickly and grab hot players who stay hot. The other side warns against boosting a fill-in starter much when a starter has a short injury, because the injury may last only a few games. It adds that bench players who post big numbers during injuries should be valued near their healthy role, about rank 150.

Our rule combines both views. If a starter's injury looks short, claim the fill-in with a small FAB bid, use him as a streamer, and drop him when the starter returns. Bid more only when the change looks lasting: a new starting job, a trade, or a long absence ahead of him. Thomas Bryant is the clearest case of upside that depends on how long the injury lasts. One big man out gives him real minutes. The expert sees top 50 to 60 upside if Allen and Mobley are both out.

Some handcuffs are worth a fast bid because the path to a big role is short. Collin Gillespie moves into a 30-minute starting role if Booker, Jalen Green or Dillon Brooks misses time. Jock Landale would start for about 30 minutes if Okongwu gets hurt, since Veesaar is out and Gueye is hurt. Joan Beringer becomes a must add if Gobert misses time.

sections.heading: Starting jobs to watch in week one

paragraphs.text: Several starting jobs are open, and each note gives a minutes line to check. At the Lakers, LaRavia, Thybulle and Ziaire Williams compete for a spot. In New Orleans it is Herbert Jones against Jeremiah Fears. In Washington, Coulibaly and Tre Johnson chase the fifth starter spot. In Phoenix, Ighodaro needs to keep starting over Maluach.

Boston has the most open battles: Scheierman against Pritchard, Hauser against Scheierman, and Mitchell Robinson against Queta at center. In Detroit, Isaiah Joe can take Duncan Robinson's starting spot. In Indiana, Nesmith must hold off Oubre. Melton and Dunn become adds if they start at about 28 minutes.

We get at most 6 acquisitions a week. Streaming for a games-played edge wins head-to-head categories. Some players here are pure streamers: Horford and Mitchell Robinson on days without back-to-backs, Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe for threes, McConnell in Indiana's 4-game weeks, and Steven Adams for rebounds in good matchups.

Do not use all 6 adds on streamers early in a week. Keep one or two open so you can react right away when a starting role changes. Streamers can be dropped. A player who wins a 28-minute starting job is worth holding.

sections.heading: Check the playoff schedule before holding

paragraphs.text: Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28. Memphis and Dallas play 4-4-4 and the Clippers play 4-3-4, which helps Spencer, Isaiah Stewart, Lively, Marshall, Sasser, Dunn, Wagler and Beal. Weaker schedules hurt others. Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week (Beringer, Hyland) and Cleveland a two-game finals week (Tyson). Brooklyn plays 3-4-3 (Minott) and Indiana 3-4-3 (McConnell). Portland has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks (Robert Williams). Houston has a 10-game schedule (Smart), and Simons faces three playoff back-to-backs.
Early-season pickups are for the weeks you are in now. By the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, favor holding players with full playoff schedules. Drop or trade the ones with two-game weeks.
